title: Keep your confidence: setbacks, comparison, culture and passing it on

say: Keep your confidence: setbacks, comparison, culture, and passing it on.
This is the video for module four of Confidence Building and Self-Belief.
Every woman who tries new things will face setbacks. With a fixed mindset, failure feels like a verdict on who you are.

panel.heading: Two ways to read a setback
left: I am not good at this
right: I am not good at this yet

say: With a growth mindset, failure is information about what to change. Add one small word: yet. I am not good at this yet.
But effort alone is not enough. Pair it with better strategies, and ask for help.

say: For example, Aisha rented a stall at a craft fair in Lagos to sell beaded jewellery. She sold only four pieces and felt like a failure. After a day to feel it, she writes a short after-action review.

say: What will I keep and change? Her colourful display worked. Next time: clear price tags, cheaper items, and a transfer account on a sign.

say: Within 48 hours she messages the eight visitors who took her card. Three order. At the next fair she sells 22 pieces.
Keep your language about the event, not about yourself.

panel.rule: I failed at this attempt is not the same as I am a failure.

say: Social media shows highlight reels, not the loans, arguments or failed attempts. For example, Grace, a teacher in Uyo, feels a sharp pang whenever a former classmate posts about her fashion business. She writes the feeling down.

panel.heading: Grace turns envy into a plan
items: Notice the envy without judging
Ask: what exactly do I want?
Turn it into a SMART goal
Congratulate her and ask how

say: What does she want? Not fashion, but extra income and the pride of running something of her own.

panel.heading: Grace turns envy into a plan
items: Notice the envy without judging
Ask: what exactly do I want?
Turn it into a SMART goal
Congratulate her and ask how

say: Her goal: weekend lessons for four primary pupils by January, using her teaching strengths.

panel.heading: Grace turns envy into a plan

Ask: what exactly do I want?
Turn it into a SMART goal
Congratulate her and ask how

say: She congratulates her classmate and asks how she got her first ten customers. By February Grace has six pupils.
Mute accounts that leave you feeling worse, and each month write three ways you have grown.

panel.rule: Compare with your past self. That comparison builds confidence.

say: You do not have to choose between respect and confidence. Think about timing, tone, channel and facts.
For example, Oluchi in Aba wants to start a shoe business in part of a family shop. Her husband's elder brothers make the decisions.

panel.heading: Oluchi speaks up wisely in the family
items: Agree the plan with her husband first
Prepare facts: costs and benefits
Choose a good time, after a meal
Open with respect, then three short points
Listen, and offer a trial

say: She agrees the plan with her husband, and prepares facts: a start-up cost of about 250,000 naira, and how profits will help with school fees.

say: Children praised only for being smart tend to avoid harder challenges. Praise the effort and the strategy instead.

panel.heading: Praise the effort, not the label

cards.d: Try: you kept trying different ways until you solved it.
Try: you are disappointed. What could you try next time?
Try: show me how you would start. I am here if you get stuck.

say: Name the feeling and point to learning. For example, Bimpe's daughter scored 9 out of 30 in maths and said, I am just not a maths person. They found most mistakes were in fractions, which she had not mastered yet.

panel.heading: Praise the effort, not the label

cards.d: Try: you kept trying different ways until you solved it.
Try: you are disappointed. What could you try next time?
Try: show me how you would start. I am here if you get stuck.

say: Let children do real, age-appropriate tasks. Tolu practised fractions four evenings a week, and three weeks later scored 18 out of 30.

say: To remember. Read setbacks as information, and act within 48 hours. Use envy to find your goal. Speak up with respect. Praise effort, and start a small circle to lift other women.

Culture never justifies violence, forced marriage or harm, and children's tasks need supervision around fire, knives, roads and money. If you feel hopeless for weeks, or anyone is at risk, get help. In an emergency, call 112.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Setbacks are information; add the word yet
Review, then act within 48 hours
Envy shows what you want; make it a goal
Respect and voice: timing, tone, channel, facts
Praise effort and lift other women

say: Now review one setback, do a comparison audit, plan how you will speak up in one situation, and invite two women to a confidence circle.
